title: Analyze User Website Visit Pattern
description:
You are given two string arrays `username` and `website` and an integer array `timestamp`, all of the same length `n`. The tuple `[username[i], timestamp[i], website[i]]` indicates that user `username[i]` visited website `website[i]` at time `timestamp[i]`.

A **pattern** is a list of **three** websites (not necessarily distinct). A user visits a pattern `(w1, w2, w3)` if they visited `w1`, then later `w2`, and then later `w3` in strictly increasing timestamp order (not necessarily consecutively).

The **score** of a pattern is the number of **distinct users** who visited all the websites in the pattern in that chronological order. (If the same user matches a pattern multiple times, that user still contributes only `1` to that pattern's score.)

Return the pattern with the **largest score**. If multiple patterns tie for the largest score, return the **lexicographically smallest** pattern (comparing element 0, then element 1, then element 2 using standard string ordering).
constraints: username[i] and website[i] consist of lowercase English letters.
It is guaranteed that there is at least one user who visited at least three websites.
No user visits two websites at the same timestamp.
hints: Input records are not guaranteed to be sorted by timestamp — group visits by username and sort each user's visits by timestamp ascending.
For each user, enumerate all 3-website combinations (i < j < k) and store them in a per-user set so each user increments a pattern's score at most once.
Track the pattern with the maximum count, breaking ties by comparing the 3-tuple of website strings lexicographically.

examples.explanation: joe visited [home, about, career], james visited [home, cart, maps, home], mary visited [home, about, career]. Pattern [home, about, career] has score 2 (joe and mary).
ua visited [a, b, a] and ub visited [a, b, c]. Both patterns have score 1, and [a, b, a] is lexicographically smaller than [a, b, c].
